description:
Auschwitz became the most infamous symbol of the Holocaust, but many of its most disturbing stories are still surprisingly unknown.
It wasn’t a single camp. Auschwitz was a vast complex of more than 40 concentration and extermination camps spread across occupied Poland. Between 1940 and 1945, approximately 1.3 million people were deported there. Around 1.1 million were murdered.

This video explores 50 facts that reveal how the system actually worked, and the people who resisted it. You’ll learn about Witold Pilecki, the Polish resistance fighter who deliberately entered Auschwitz to report on the killings from inside. The women who secretly smuggled gunpowder grain by grain to help destroy Crematorium IV. The prisoner orchestras, tattoo system, “Kanada” warehouses filled with victims’ possessions, Mengele’s experiments, mass escapes, death marches, and the SS attempt to destroy the evidence before liberation.
